rationale: hammernik_vn iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). LAST-LEVER / confirmation iter. ONE KNOB on the REGULARIZER (not capacity, not lambda): vn_normalize_filters False -> True (constrain each learned filter K_i to zero-mean + unit-norm, the paper-faithful constraint, solver _effective_weight lines 119-128). All else held at iter-3 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_lambda_init=0.05, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, all BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (vn_n_filters=16, elapsed 1295.7s); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (vn_n_filters=24, capacity UP -> REGRESSED -0.0133, elapsed 1351.7s); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05, DC-weight ~22x UP -> REGRESSED -0.0238, elapsed 1159.6s, val_psnr 32.07, val_rmse 1.246e-3). BOTH structural levers already attacked the wrong thing: capacity-UP regressed AND DC-weight-UP regressed, so the recon sits monotonically BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). FAILURE MODE (well-characterized): the learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i u) is a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline, and it does so REGARDLESS of capacity (filters^ hurt) or DC weight (lambda^ hurt). This FIRES iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier: 'if SSIM stays <=0.84 under strong DC, the VN regulariser is structurally degrading -> iter-4 attacks the regulariser itself: vn_normalize_filters=True OR vn_init=backproj'. CHOICE OF KNOB (most diagnostic remaining): vn_normalize_filters=True is the SHARPEST test of the smoothing diagnosis, and is preferred over vn_init=backproj (which changes only the init, not the regularizer mechanism, and the baseline is pinned to FBP either way). MECHANISM: zero-mean filters have NO DC response -- conv with a zero-mean kernel annihilates any uniform/low-frequency level component -- so a zero-mean-unit-norm-constrained K_i CANNOT apply a uniform smoothing or level shift to the image; the regulariser term can only act on local CONTRAST (edges/texture). Unit-norm caps each filter's gain so no single filter can dominate and over-smooth. If the iter-1/2/3 degradation was the unconstrained filters collapsing to a DC/low-pass smoother, this constraint removes that failure path -> the recon should stop sinking below the FBP init and hr should rise toward / above 0. HYPOTHESIS: with zero-mean unit-norm filters the regulariser stops smoothing the FBP init below baseline; val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr > 0). FALSIFIER (the terminal one): if val_ssim still <= 0.84 (below FBP) with the regulariser CONSTRAINED, then hammernik_vn is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on rebinned Mayo regardless of regulariser config (capacity, DC weight, AND filter constraint all exhausted) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT: the Hammernik-VN learned-regulariser family does not beat LD-FBP on real 2304-view Mayo LDCT, and drive the remaining iters to document the ceiling, not chase it. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the zero-mean/unit-norm normalization is a cheap per-step reshape (filter tensor is (24,1,11,11)); per-step forward/back-project DC cost is IDENTICAL to iter-3, so wall ~= iter-3 (1159.6s) -- well under the 1800s SLURM kill, ~640s margin. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-3 -- batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=24 within the 16 GB RTX5000 (no OOM; cf. the hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM at 72s). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise).
